title: Hidden patterns of urban mixing across five global cities
authors: Zhuangyuan Fan; Becky P. Y. Loo; Fabio Duarte; Carlo Ratti; Esteban Moro
abstract: Here we leverage large-scale travel surveys covering over 200,000 residents across Boston, Chicago, Hong Kong, London and São Paulo. With rich individual-level data, we reveal patterns in social mixing, which cannot be identified from high-resolution mobility data alone. Inferring socioeconomic status from residential neighborhoods yields social mixing levels 16% lower than using survey data. Individuals over the age of 66 experience greater social mixing than those in late working life (aged 55–65), lending data-driven support to the ‘second youth’ hypothesis. Teenagers and women with caregiving responsibilities exhibit lower social mixing levels. Living near major transit stations reduces the influence of socioeconomic status on social mixing. Finally, inputs of home-space, activity-space and demographic attributes are embedded and fed into a supervised autoencoder, revealing that mobility shapes experienced social mixing more than sociodemographic characteristics, home environment and transit proximity. Yet, activity spaces remain stratified by income, resulting in structurally different social mixing experiences. Using travel surveys from five global cities, this study explores how daily mobility shapes social mixing. Results show that activity spaces explain most place exposure variations, outweighing demographics and transit proximity.
abstractZh: 本文利用覆盖波士顿、芝加哥、香港、伦敦和圣保罗20多万居民的大规模出行调查。凭借丰富的个体层面数据，揭示仅靠高分辨率移动数据无法识别的社会混合模式。根据居住邻里推断社会经济地位，得到的社会混合水平比使用调查数据低16%。66岁以上个体经历的社会混合高于职业生涯后期人群（55—65岁），为“第二青春”假说提供数据支持。青少年和承担照护责任的女性社会混合水平较低。居住在主要公交站点附近，会减弱社会经济地位对社会混合的影响。最后，将居住空间、活动空间和人口属性嵌入并输入有监督自编码器，发现移动对体验社会混合的塑造作用，大于社会人口特征、居住环境和公共交通邻近性。然而，活动空间仍然按收入分层，导致结构不同的社会混合体验。本研究利用五个全球城市的出行调查，考察每日移动如何塑造社会混合，结果显示活动空间解释了场所暴露差异的主要部分，其作用超过人口特征和公共交通邻近性。
summary: 跨五城市调查揭示收入标签和日程对混合测量的影响
